toolchain_note: Pylint 3.3.1 with a self-contained astroid-based plugin loaded via --load-plugins; the plugin is embedded in smell_check.sh so no repository file is needed to run it.

rule.description: A concrete in-repo class that explicitly inherits an in-repo interface (a typing.Protocol style base, or a base whose own method bodies are pure raise-NotImplementedError declarations) with at least two implementors must not be forced to carry interface methods that no reachable production call path can invoke on that implementor; each such obligation means the interface exceeds the implementor's dependency boundary.

detection_semantics.interface_identification: An in-repo class is an interface when it has Protocol among its bases or declares at least one of its own methods as a pure raise-NotImplementedError body, and at least two other in-repo classes inherit from it through the in-repo base chain. Only root interfaces are analyzed; obligations that a derived interface adds are credited to the root.
detection_semantics.implementor_gates: Obligations are reported only for classes that production code actually instantiates (a concrete class applied to a call, a module-level assignment's right-hand side, or a class returned by a factory) and that are neither interfaces nor abstract bases.
detection_semantics.usage_analysis: A method counts as used on an implementor when at least one production call site can dispatch it on that class. Receivers are resolved by name: a module variable maps to the set of classes it can hold (direct instantiation, or the union of classes a module-level factory returns); a self-receiver inside a class maps to that class plus its in-repo subclasses. Tests, examples, and e2e code are not production and cannot make a method used.
detection_semantics.consumers_that_provide_usage: mesop/runtime/context.py (state restore/save over the state-session singleton), mesop/server/server.py (cookie redemption over the cookie store singleton, teardown sweep over the state-session singleton), mesop/server/server_utils.py (state-token minting over the state-session singleton), plus internal self-calls in the file backend (token admission) and in the msgpack backends (state codec).

checks.description: Detects a store that queues browser cookies being forced to carry application-state persistence.
checks.detected_relation: _CookieTokenCache -- must provide --> SessionBackend.restore/save, but no production call path can invoke restore/save on _CookieTokenCache.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The interface exceeds the implementor's dependency boundary: a cache for one-time cookie nonces is made to depend on serialized-state persistence.

matches.evidence: _CookieTokenCache.restore only raises MesopException; the singleton that could dispatch restore holds state-session backends, never the cookie store.
_CookieTokenCache.save only raises MesopException; the singleton that could dispatch save holds state-session backends, never the cookie store.

checks.description: Detects a store being forced to carry session garbage collection although production sweeps only the state-session singleton.
checks.detected_relation: _CookieTokenCache -- must provide --> SessionBackend.clear_stale_sessions, but no production call path can invoke clear_stale_sessions on _CookieTokenCache.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The tail-request sweep exists to bound state storage; the cookie store repurposes the same obligation to fold in a nonce eviction that pop already performs.

matches.evidence: clear_stale_sessions on _CookieTokenCache is unreachable: teardown sweeps the state-session singleton only.

checks.description: Detects a store being forced to carry state-token minting although it mints its own redemption nonce inline.
checks.detected_relation: _CookieTokenCache -- must provide --> SessionBackend.issue_token, but no production call path can invoke issue_token on _CookieTokenCache.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Minting tokens for state restoration is a state-session concern; the cookie store creates and stores its nonce inside put.

matches.evidence: issue_token on _CookieTokenCache is dead code: production mints the redemption nonce inside _CookieTokenCache.put.

checks.description: Detects implementors forced to carry the interface's token-admission predicate although nothing can invoke it on them.
checks.detected_relation: state-session backend / cookie store -- must provide --> SessionBackend.validate_token, but only the filesystem backend calls validate_token on itself and no external receiver can dispatch it on these classes.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A single validity contract is imposed broadly, while each store actually admits tokens through its own lookup (dict hit, file path check, Firestore document get, SQL select, pop-time signature freshness).

matches.evidence: NullStateSessionBackend never validates tokens; restore refuses immediately, so validate_token can never run on it.
MemoryStateSessionBackend never validates tokens; dict membership on restore is the real admission check.
FirestoreStateSessionBackend never validates tokens; document lookup determines admission.
SqlStateSessionBackend never validates tokens; the SQL select determines admission.
_CookieTokenCache never validates tokens; pop enforces one-time use and freshness instead.

checks.description: Detects implementors forced to carry the interface's dataclass encode/decode codec although they never serialize state.
checks.detected_relation: Null/MemoryStateSessionBackend and _CookieTokenCache -- must provide --> SessionBackend.encode_states/decode_states, but the codec only executes on the msgpack backends (file, Firestore, SQL) via their own self-calls.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The serialization codec belongs to stores that persist serialized payloads; stores that hold live objects or cookie payloads are made to depend on dataclass marshalling they never perform.

matches.evidence: decode_states can never run on the no-op backend; nothing calls it on a state-session receiver.
encode_states can never run on the no-op backend; nothing calls it on a state-session receiver.
decode_states can never run on the in-memory backend; restore copies stored objects directly.
encode_states can never run on the in-memory backend; save stores the live state objects.
decode_states can never run on the cookie store; it stores signed cookie payloads, not application state.
encode_states can never run on the cookie store; it stores signed cookie payloads, not application state.

checks.description: Detects state-session backends forced to carry the pending-cookie redemption pair although only the cookie store queues and redeems cookies.
checks.detected_relation: Null/Memory/File/Firestore/SqlStateSessionBackend -- must provide --> SessionBackend.put/pop, but the only production receivers of put/pop are the module-level cookie store.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Cookie redemption is a browser-set-cookie capability unrelated to state persistence; every state backend is made to depend on it (and refuses it at runtime), which is the fat-interface obligation.

matches.evidence: pop inherited by NullStateSessionBackend can never execute; the /__apply-cookies route only talks to the cookie store.
put inherited by NullStateSessionBackend can never execute; no production code queues cookies on a state backend.
pop inherited by MemoryStateSessionBackend can never execute; the /__apply-cookies route only talks to the cookie store.
put inherited by MemoryStateSessionBackend can never execute; no production code queues cookies on a state backend.
pop inherited by FileStateSessionBackend can never execute; the /__apply-cookies route only talks to the cookie store.
put inherited by FileStateSessionBackend can never execute; no production code queues cookies on a state backend.
pop inherited by FirestoreStateSessionBackend can never execute; the /__apply-cookies route only talks to the cookie store.
put inherited by FirestoreStateSessionBackend can never execute; no production code queues cookies on a state backend.
pop inherited by SqlStateSessionBackend can never execute; the /__apply-cookies route only talks to the cookie store.
put inherited by SqlStateSessionBackend can never execute; no production code queues cookies on a state backend.

excluded.reason: The declared interface itself: the rule reports the implementors it forces to carry unused methods, not the interface declaration.
Abstract template base: production never constructs it and it declares abstract methods, so it is not a concrete implementor carrying obligations.
Removed helper: token minting is re-homed behind the interface; the production call site is a consumer, not an implementor.
A Protocol with no in-repo implementors is outside this rule: the smell requires implementors forced to carry methods they cannot use.
Test modules are not production code and cannot make a method used for this rule.
